# Project Overview

This project evaluates the cycling network connectivity of Belfast using the
**Level of Traffic Stress (LTS)** framework (Mekuria et al. 2012) and the
**Percent Trips Connected** metric. I built this as my contribution to the
[PCTNI Data-Driven Transport Planning Hackathon](https://pctni.github.io/hack/)
(18 May 2026, hosted by Prof. Robin Lovelace at Queen's University Belfast).

The central question is straightforward: **if you only use low-stress roads,
how much of Belfast's commuting demand can you actually serve?**

### What I Did

I classified every cyclable road segment in Belfast into four stress levels
(LTS 1–4) based on speed limits, lane counts, and cycling infrastructure,
following the Conveyal/Mekuria framework augmented by Jeong & Smith (2025).
I then computed network connectivity — for each pair of Super Data Zones, I
checked whether a low-stress route exists that doesn't require an unreasonable
detour compared to the shortest path.

### Key Findings

The results reveal severe fragmentation in Belfast's low-stress cycling network:

- At **LTS ≤ 1** (suitable for children): only **0.0%** of commuting trips connected
- At **LTS ≤ 2** (tolerable for most adults): only **0.7%**
- At **LTS ≤ 3** (experienced cyclists): **7.9%**
- At **LTS ≤ 4** (all roads): **100%**

This means Belfast has plenty of quiet residential streets, but they don't form
a connected network — cyclists are forced onto high-stress arterials to complete
their journeys.

### Data Sources

- **Road network**: OpenStreetMap via pyrosm (LTS classification) and OSMnx (graph topology)
- **Commuting demand**: Census 2021 OD flows (ODWP01) at Super Data Zone level, from the [PCTNI hackathon datasets](https://github.com/pctni/hack/releases/tag/v0.1.0)
- **Zone boundaries**: NISRA Super Data Zones 2021
